gbm_population_evidence.quote: Recurrent Glioblastoma; Recurrent WHO Grade 4 Glioma
Recurrent World Health Organization (WHO) grade IV glioblastoma.

candidate_evidence.quote: Patients receive retifanlimab IV over 30 minutes on day 1 and bevacizumab IV on day 1 and 15 of each cycle.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Recurrent Glioblastoma; Recurrent WHO Grade 4 Glioma

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: To assess the anti-glioma immune response before and after retifanlimab including assessment of immune cells phenotyping, function and activation in the pre-/post-treatment blood, and changes in cytokine levels over time.

role_evidence.quote: compared to bevacizumab and hypofractionated radiotherapy alone

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: Immunotherapy with monoclonal antibodies, such as retifanlimab, may help the body's immune system attack the cancer

role_evidence.quote: ARM B: Patients receive bevacizumab IV on day 1 and 15 of each cycle.

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: Bevacizumab is in a class of medications called antiangiogenic agents.

coder_notes: Both arms are registered EXPERIMENTAL; Arm B (bevacizumab + HFRT) works as the control. Bevacizumab is given identically in both arms, so soc_backbone (not the question). cns5_terminology coded historical because the condition is WHO Grade 4 Glioma without an IDH requirement, although eligibility also mentions 'molecular GBM'.
